edges.description: Systemic viral dissemination and mild rotavirus-induced hepatic injury cause transient elevations of serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST).
Elevated cytosolic calcium gates apical calcium-activated chloride channels and inhibits electroneutral NaCl absorption.
NSP4-induced calcium signaling triggers paracrine 5-HT release from enteroendocrine cells that activates enteric secretomotor reflexes.
Transepithelial chloride secretion and osmotic water movement into the small intestinal lumen produce profuse watery secretory diarrhea.
Excessive luminal water and electrolyte secretion leads to rapid volume depletion in infants and young children.
Stool electrolyte and bicarbonate losses during profuse secretory diarrhea cause metabolic acidosis.
Enteric secretomotor reflex activation sustains transepithelial chloride and water secretion across the small intestinal mucosa.
Serotonin-mediated activation of vagal afferent pathways projecting to brainstem emetic centers induces acute vomiting.
Enteric nervous system activation and increased small intestinal motility cause cramping abdominal pain.
Loss of mature villus enterocytes and proteasomal DGAT1 degradation deplete apical brush-border disaccharidases (particularly lactase), impairing lactose and carbohydrate digestion.

nodes.description: NSP4-induced elevation of cytosolic free calcium activates calcium-gated chloride channels (including ANO1/TMEM16A) on the apical membrane of intestinal epithelial cells, driving transepithelial halide and chloride ion secretion into the gut lumen and creating an osmotic gradient that draws water into the lumen independently of cyclic nucleotides (cAMP/cGMP). Because rotavirus does not infect all enterocytes, sodium-glucose cotransporter 1 (SGLT1) function remains intact across uninfected enterocytes, enabling oral rehydration therapy.

nodes.description: Following cellular uptake, rotavirus genome replication and virion assembly take place in specialized cytoplasmic inclusions termed viroplasms, and progeny virions are released by enterocyte lysis or non-classical vesicular transport. nodes.description: Rotavirus infection and NSP4-mediated intracellular calcium elevation stimulate serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5-HT) secretion from enteroendocrine (enterochromaffin) cells in the small intestine. evidence.snippet: Rotavirus infection and NSP4-mediated increase in intracellular calcium levels can induce secretion of 5-HT from enteroendocrine cells in humans and mice, which can activate enteric nerves that innervate the small intestine and ultimately lead to increased intestinal motility

nodes.description: Rotavirus nonstructural protein 4 (NSP4) is the first described viral enterotoxin. Acting both endogenously as an endoplasmic reticulum viroporin in infected cells and exogenously as a secreted enterotoxin that binds uninfected intestinal epithelial cells and signals through phospholipase C (PLC) and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3), NSP4 increases cytoplasmic free calcium levels and coordinates downstream ion transport changes.

nodes.description: First-line supportive therapy consists of reduced-osmolarity (245 mOsm/L) oral rehydration salts (ORS) containing equimolar glucose (75 mmol/L) and sodium (75 mEq/L) plus potassium and base (citrate or bicarbonate), exploiting preserved SGLT1-mediated glucose-coupled sodium and water absorption across uninfected small intestinal enterocytes to prevent and reverse dehydration and metabolic acidosis.

evidence.snippet: One of the most important medical advancements in the past 50 years that has saved millions of infant lives was that administration of ORS resulted in glucose-coupled sodium and water absorption in the small intestine137. nodes.description: Rotavirus infection induces proteasome-dependent degradation of diacylglycerol O-acyltransferase 1 (DGAT1) and increases phosphorylation of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 alpha (eIF2alpha) in infected enterocytes. Loss of DGAT1 and global translational arrest downregulate apical brush-border enzymes (including lactase, sucrase, and maltase), disrupt enterocyte lipid droplet and membrane homeostasis, and cause cytolysis and desquamation of mature villus tip enterocytes with reactive crypt hyperplasia. Unabsorbed luminal disaccharides and solutes create an osmotic gradient that drives malabsorptive osmotic diarrhea.

nodes.description: Oral live-attenuated rotavirus vaccination—including monovalent human attenuated G1P[8] vaccine (RV1, Rotarix) and pentavalent bovine-human reassortant G1, G2, G3, G4, P1A[8] vaccine (RV5, RotaTeq)—administered in early infancy induces intestinal secretory IgA and homotypic and heterotypic serum neutralizing antibodies targeting the outer capsid proteins VP7 and VP4 (VP8*/VP5*) as well as non-neutralizing mucosal anti-VP6 and anti-NSP4 immunity. Mucosal and systemic immunity blocks viral attachment and entry into villus enterocytes and neutralizes NSP4 enterotoxin activity, preventing severe dehydrating secretory and malabsorptive gastroenteritis.

evidence.snippet: Two rotavirus vaccines are broadly used worldwide: the RV5 vaccine, RotaTeq (Merck, USA), and the RV1 vaccine, Rotarix (GlaxoSmithKline, Belgium). The RV5 vaccine is a live attenuated, pentavalent vaccine, which is composed of five bovine–human reassortant rotaviruses that express either human VP4 or VP7 from rotavirus strains G1, G2, G3, G4
Both vaccines are highly effective in preventing severe rotavirus disease in high-income countries117 but reduce the incidence of severe rotavirus disease by ~50–60% in many low-income countries

nodes.description: During the first 5 days of acute rotavirus gastroenteritis, viral antigens (antigenemia, reported in one study in at least 90% of acutely infected children) and infectious virions (viremia) enter the bloodstream across the damaged intestinal barrier. Antigenemia correlates with higher acute gastroenteritis severity and limited extraintestinal viral dissemination, including mild rotavirus-associated hepatitis with transient elevation of serum hepatic transaminases (ALT and AST), though direct causal links between antigenemia and other extraintestinal presentations remain unestablished in human cohorts.

evidence.snippet: Detection of viral antigens (that is, antigenaemia) and infectious viruses (that is, viraemia) in serum have been reported in children with rotavirus infection, and replication of rotavirus in sites other than the intestines, although limited, is likely to occur
One study reported antigenaemia in ≥90% of children with rotavirus infection until ~5 days after symptom onset, and some children had infectious virus in their serum

In other studies, children with antigenaemia had more severe disease than children without antigenaemia, but the proportion of children with extra-intestinal presentations was not higher in those with antigenaemia

nodes.description: Oral zinc supplementation (10-20 mg daily for 10-14 days) administered as an adjunct to oral rehydration therapy restores intestinal mucosal barrier integrity, reduces stool output, and shortens the duration of diarrhea, vomiting, and fever in children with rotaviral enteritis, particularly in low-income settings with a high burden of malnutrition.

evidence.snippet: Conventional therapy combined with the zinc preparation significantly shortened the duration of hyperthermia, vomiting, and diarrhea compared with the conventional treatment alone.
In addition, zinc supplementation can improve the outcome of acute diarrhoea in low-income regions, in which malnutrition is common.
For children living in low-income regions, the WHO recommends daily zinc supplementation for infants and children for 10–14 days, starting as soon as the diarrhoea episode has been diagnosed
